Part B of title IV of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 284 et seq.), as amended by section 1001 of this Act, is amended by adding at the end the following:

“SEC. 409E. AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES.
“(a) Expansion, Intensification, and Coordination of Activities.—
“(1) In general.—The Director of NIH shall expand, intensify, and coordinate research and other activities of the National Institutes of Health with respect to autoimmune diseases.
“(2) Allocations by director of nih.—With respect to amounts appropriated to carry out this section for a fiscal year, the Director of NIH shall allocate the amounts among the national research institutes that are carrying out paragraph (1).
“(3) Definition.—The term ‘autoimmune disease’ includes, for purposes of this section such diseases or disorders with evidence of autoimmune pathogens is as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.
“(b) Coordinating Committee.—
“(1) In general.—The Secretary shall ensure that the Autoimmune Diseases Coordinating Committee (referred to in this section as the ‘Coordinating Committee’) coordinates activities across the National Institutes and with other Federal health programs and activities relating to such diseases.
“(2) Composition.—The Coordinating Committee shall be composed of the directors or their designees of each of the national research institutes involved in research with respect to autoimmune diseases and representatives of all other Federal departments and agencies whose programs involve health functions or responsibilities relevant to such diseases, including the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration.
“(3) Chair.—
“(A) In general.—With respect to autoimmune diseases, the Chair of the Committee shall serve as the principal advisor to the Secretary, the Assistant Secretary for Health, and the Director of NIH, and shall provide advice to the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, and other relevant agencies.
“(B) Director of nih.—The Chair of the Committee shall be directly responsible to the Director of NIH.
“(c) Plan for NIH Activities.—
“(1) In general.—Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this section, the Coordinating Committee shall develop a plan for conducting and supporting research and education on autoimmune diseases through the national research institutes and shall periodically review and revise the plan. The plan shall—

“(A) provide for a broad range of research and education activities relating to biomedical, psychosocial, and rehabilitative issues, including studies of the disproportionate impact of such diseases on women;
“(B) identify priorities among the programs and activities of the National Institutes of Health regarding such diseases; and
“(C) reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups.
“(2) Certain elements of plan.—The plan under paragraph (1) shall, with respect to autoimmune diseases, provide for the following as appropriate:
“(A) Research to determine the reasons underlying the incidence and prevalence of the diseases.
“(B) Basic research concerning the etiology and causes of the diseases.
“(C) Epidemiological studies to address the frequency and natural history of the diseases, including any differences among the sexes and among racial and ethnic groups.
“(D) The development of improved screening techniques.
“(E) Clinical research for the development and evaluation of new treatments, including new biological agents.
“(F) Information and education programs for health care professionals and the public.
“(3) Implementation of plan.—The Director of NIH shall ensure that programs and activities of the National Institutes of Health regarding autoimmune diseases are implemented in accordance with the plan under paragraph (1).
“(d) Reports to Congress.—The Coordinating Committee under subsection (b)(1) shall biennially submit to the Committee on Commerce of the House of Representatives, and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions of the Senate, a report that describes the research, education, and other activities on autoimmune diseases being conducted or supported through the national research institutes, and that in addition includes the following:
“(1) The plan under subsection (c)(1) (or revisions to the plan, as the case may be).
“(2) Provisions specifying the amounts expended by the National Institutes of Health with respect to each of the autoimmune diseases included in the plan.
“(3) Provisions identifying particular projects or types of projects that should in the future be considered by the national research institutes or other entities in the field of research on autoimmune diseases.
“(e) Authorization of Appropriations.—For the purpose of carrying out this section, there are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary for each of the fiscal years 2001 through 2005. The authorization of appropriations established in the preceding sentence is in addition to any other authorization of appropriations that is available for conducting or supporting through the National Institutes of Health research and other activities with respect to autoimmune diseases.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is "No" because the Coordinating Committee is composed entirely of federal officials and the section also includes reports to Congress, both of which stay inside the government. However, the plan the Committee develops must reflect input from scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, who are outside the federal government. That plan sets NIH priorities and the Director must implement programs in accordance with it, so it is a federal decision shaped by outside input rather than a mere study.
fable.s: reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups

opus.w: The Coordinating Committee's plan, which sets NIH research priorities and which the Director of NIH must follow, has to reflect input from scientists, patients, and advocacy groups, all of whom are outside the federal government. That brings outsiders into a federal decision. The all-federal membership of the Committee and the reports to congressional committees stay inside the government and would not count on their own. And unlike the study in Example 3, this plan binds how NIH carries out its programs.

1. **The tempting reading, and why it's incomplete.** It's tempting to answer "No" here. The Coordinating Committee is made up entirely of NIH institute directors and representatives of other federal agencies, so that is coordination inside the government. The reports go to congressional committees, which are also inside the government. Neither crosses the federal boundary. But the plan has to "reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups." Those groups are outside the government. The plan is also more than a study, unlike Example 3: it "identif[ies] priorities among the programs and activities" of NIH, and the Director of NIH must carry out NIH's programs in line with it. So outsiders feed into a federal decision about research priorities.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a Coordinating Committee composed entirely of federal officials (directors of NIH institutes and representatives of other federal agencies). While subsection (c)(1)(C) mentions that the plan should 'reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups,' this is a substantive requirement for the plan's content rather than a procedural mandate for the government to consult or coordinate with these outside parties before making a decision. There is no requirement for public hearings, comment periods, or advisory boards with non-federal members. The primary decision-making body is internal to the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: (2) Composition.—The Coordinating Committee shall be composed of the directors or their designees of each of the national research institutes involved in research with respect to autoimmune diseases and representatives of all other Federal departments and agencies whose programs involve health functions or responsibilities relevant to such diseases, including the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue "Yes" because subsection (c)(1)(C) states the plan shall "reflect input from a broad range of scientists, patients, and advocacy groups." However, this language is vague ("reflect input") and does not explicitly mandate a specific participatory mechanism (like a hearing, comment period, or advisory board with outside members) for that input. More importantly, the primary structure of the section establishes an internal coordinating committee composed entirely of federal officials (subsection (b)(2)). The "input" requirement is a soft directive for the content of the plan, not a procedural requirement for outside participation in the decision-making process itself. The definition requires that the government *consult or coordinate* with outsiders *before* making a decision. While the plan must reflect input, the statute does not prescribe *how* that input is gathered (e.g., it doesn't require a public hearing or a formal consultation process). It is more likely an internal directive to consider existing knowledge. Furthermore, the Coordinating Committee itself is internal. The "input" clause is the only potential hook, but it is weak. Let's look closer. "Reflect input from..." is not "consult with...". It could mean reviewing literature. It does not mandate interaction. Therefore, "No" is the safer, more accurate label based on the strict definition of "consult or coordinate... before making a decision". The committee is internal. The report is to Congress (internal). The plan is developed by the internal committee. The "input" is not procedurally defined as participation.
